paragraphs: Decision center: the core work of dermatologists is to make judgments about skin findings that are visible to the naked eye but may have systemic causes — starting from a complete skin examination and history, deciding which findings are malignant lesions that must be excluded immediately, which are chronic conditions manageable long term with topical or systemic drugs, which require biopsy, surgery, laser or phototherapy, and which should be referred to another specialty. The focus is not “whether you like looking at skin” but whether, along the chain of look, ask, examine, take and treat, follow up, every case can be made reviewable and accountable.

Editorial observation suggestion: verify the medical education and practice pathway and experience detailed recording, repeated verification and communication; whether you have patience for long-term follow-up and complete records is confirmed by training and mentoring feedback, and short consultation times or interest labels are not used to predict ability.

Editorial verification suggestion: the target position's patient volume, on-call duty, exposure and protection requirements, and the medical education and training time you can invest should all be understood first. The available sources give no representative Chinese sample of seeing dozens of patients a day, so it cannot be asserted that the actual experience will necessarily differ from expectations.

Low-cost experience: complete the full fictitious document exercise D-05 below, reading the outpatient record v1 and the handover draft v2, list two blanks and four conflicts, retain the original versions and write the handover pending verification. The reference answers are six textual differences; observe verification and recording preferences, and do not judge disease, order examinations, choose medication or work on real people.

Decision center: whether one can turn what was seen in one dermatology consultation into a diagnosis and treatment plan that the patient understands, that peers can review and that can be tracked afterwards, and take responsibility for the risk of missed diagnosis.

The actual environment is verified by position. Among O*NET U.S. subcategory respondents, 81% report daily indoor controlled environment, 72% close physical contact distance, 71% daily disease or infection exposure and 95% daily protective equipment. These are not the share of all dermatologists in daily contact with specific exudates or ulcers; outpatient, procedural, ward and teaching divisions are verified separately by institution.

On this page the U.S. SOC29-1213.00 diagnoses and treats diseases of the skin, hair and nails and may also practise dermatologic surgery; aesthetic medicine is only a possible direction. Pathology, surgery, general practice, internal medicine, nursing and technical positions each have their own outputs; the ability to diagnose, prescribe or operate a laser must not be assumed from the occupational title, and is verified against the target jurisdiction, registration and unit authorization.

Inputs that must be verified: chief complaint and course of illness, past history and medication and allergy history, occupational and sun exposure history, family history (especially skin tumours), records of lesion site and morphology (including photographs or descriptions), previous treatment response, and whether pathological or laboratory examination is needed. What must not be done: do not provide care without practice qualification or beyond registered practice scope, do not treat suspicious lesions as benign first on insufficient evidence, do not omit the decision to biopsy and send for pathology, do not omit informed consent and medical records, and do not perform surgery or laser treatment without the corresponding authorization.

Fit judgments should combine clinical mentoring observation and feedback from pathology and follow-up results, and are not replaced by an interest type or a single test; morphology recognition ability, the habit of verifying in a short time, and tolerance in long-term communication with patients with chronic disease must all be confirmed in real training and feedback.

The paper exercises on this page all use fictitious materials; independent practice must meet the target jurisdiction's qualification, registration, practice scope and unit authorization, and formal training must follow the applicable guidance system. Where aesthetic medicine is involved, the attending physician conditions, individual specialty filing and institutional project admission must be verified separately, and these permissions cannot be obtained through text exercises.

The work objects of this occupation are the patient's skin, hair and nail findings and the related systemic condition: chief complaint and course of illness, lesion morphology and distribution, previous treatment and medication history, sun and occupational exposure history, and family history; the outputs are diagnostic and differential considerations, treatment plans and informed consent, topical and systemic medication records, biopsy and pathology requests, surgical or physical treatment records, and follow-up and education records; the basis for judgment is dermatology standards and guidelines, pathology and imaging results, drug and device instructions, and the unit's clinical policies, not the institution's name.

Check one: whether the history and lesion records are complete — whether the course, site, morphology, evolution, medication and topical use history have been verified clearly; missing items must be pursued or supplemented by examination, without drawing conclusions from impressions.

Editorial verification question: are the patient information and the diagnostic basis such as physical examination and pathology complete, and are there missing items or conflicts requiring an authorized physician's supplementary judgment, consultation or referral? Care is decided by actual indications and standards, and the paper exercise does not judge malignancy or biopsy on its own.

Editorial clinical verification: explain the condition, the medical measures and the matters that should be disclosed to the patient; for surgery, special examinations or special treatments, explain the risks and alternatives in specific terms and obtain explicit consent. Where aesthetic medicine applies, written disclosure and signature follow article 19 separately, and not all daily conversation is standardised as a surgical consent procedure.

Check four: whether the procedures are within one's own practice scope and authorization — whether biopsy, excision, laser, phototherapy and aesthetic dermatology procedures fall within one's registered practice scope, training experience and unit authorization; when beyond it, refer or involve a supervising physician according to the process.

Check five: whether infection control and protection are in place — whether hand hygiene, protective equipment, instrument and equipment disinfection, and the handling of infectious skin disease and body fluid exposure are carried out according to standards.

Check six: whether follow-up and education form a closed loop — whether recall and plan adjustment for chronic disease, sun protection and self-examination education, postoperative precautions and suture removal arrangements, and pathology result return and management of abnormalities are recorded and implemented.

The work of dermatologists can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is receiving patients and diagnosis: consultation and history verification, complete skin examination and hair and nail examination, and where necessary dermoscopy, Wood's lamp or pathology and laboratory examination to form a diagnosis and differential considerations, then developing a treatment plan and alternatives and obtaining informed consent after explanation. The second is treatment and procedures: prescribing topical and systemic medication according to indications and arranging monitoring, performing biopsy, excision of superficial masses, cryotherapy, laser, phototherapy or chemical peels and similar procedures, managing intraoperative problems, collaborating with pathology, laboratory testing or related specialties when necessary, and recording each time. The third is follow-up and education: evaluating outcomes and adverse reactions, adjusting plans, arranging recalls, providing sun protection and skin self-examination education, returning pathology and examination results and managing abnormalities. The three work areas alternate; outpatient work predominates, but hospital positions may also involve ward consultation, difficult case discussion and resident mentoring.

This table compares dermatology with related positions by objects, process, outputs and responsibility. Pathologists analyse specimens, issue reports and collaborate with clinicians, and O*NET also lists biopsy sampling; general practice and internal medicine cover other health problems; nursing and technical positions work according to their own qualifications and policies, and it is not the case that names prohibit all diagnosis nationwide or grant equipment operating rights. Aesthetic medicine attending physician conditions and institutional projects are verified separately, and authority cannot be swapped by institution name.
Core purpose

Diagnose visible findings on the skin, hair and nails, exclude or confirm malignant lesions, and keep the condition within an acceptable range using medication, procedures and long-term management, while taking responsibility for adverse reactions and follow-up.

Related outputs include pathology reports, surgical and follow-up records, diagnosis and treatment of systemic disease, nursing observation and approved equipment operating records; duties are determined by one's own qualification, jurisdiction and institution, and the names “technician” or “aesthetic practitioner” are not treated as clinical licensure.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the patient's skin, hair and nail findings and the related systemic condition; the basis is dermatology standards and guidelines, dermoscopy and pathology and laboratory results, drug and device instructions, and the unit's clinical policies.

Objects and basis of adjacent and related positions: pathological specimens and slides (pathology diagnostic standards); body surface masses, complex wounds and reconstruction needs (surgical and plastic surgery standards); laboratory and imaging tests for systemic disease (internal medicine standards); orders and nursing routines (nursing policy); equipment parameters and treatment plans (technical operating procedures); and aesthetic medicine indications and contraindications (the Measures for the Administration of Medical Aesthetic Services and the project classification catalogue).
Core process

Consultation and physical examination → lesion morphology records and auxiliary examinations → diagnosis and differential → treatment plan and informed consent → medication and procedural treatment → return of pathology and follow-up results → plan adjustment and education.

Processes of adjacent and related positions: sampling, slide preparation and microscopy with report issuance (pathologists); preoperative assessment, excision and repair and postoperative management (surgery and plastic surgery); systemic disease assessment and medication adjustment (internal medicine); executing orders, dressing changes and observation (nursing); operating equipment according to plan and recording parameters (technicians); assessing indications and performing procedures (aesthetic medicine).
Main outputs

Outpatient records and lesion descriptions, diagnosis and differential considerations, prescriptions and medication monitoring records, biopsy and pathology requests, procedure and surgical records, follow-up and education records, and consultation and referral opinions.

Outputs of adjacent and related positions: histopathology reports; surgical records and postoperative follow-up; systemic disease diagnosis and treatment records; nursing and procedure records; equipment treatment parameters and outcome records; aesthetic medicine project informed consent and follow-up records.
Responsible party

The personnel in this occupation are responsible for the diagnosis, the timing of biopsy and pathology judgment, treatment choice and procedural quality, informed consent and medical records; matters involving other specialties must be handled by consultation or referral according to the process, and one's own authorization must not be interpreted expansively.

Each position is responsible according to its qualification and scope. Where medical aesthetics applies, article 11 requires the aesthetic dermatology attending physician to have licensed physician qualification and registration and at least 3 years of dermatology clinical experience, with qualified medical aesthetics training or further study, or at least 1 year of aesthetic medicine clinical experience, plus other provincial conditions; the training and the 1-year branch are alternative, and the remaining conditions are cumulative. Under article 12, a licensed physician not meeting the attending conditions may provide services under the attending physician's direction. The 2017 notice has the institution determine the attending specialty, file with the department issuing the institution's certificate and note it on the certificate, with the original registration information unchanged. Article 29 provides that aesthetic activities involved in the treatment of diseases in the relevant clinical disciplines do not fall under these measures, so all disease-treatment lasers cannot be classified uniformly as aesthetic attending work.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with pathology, laboratory testing, imaging and radiotherapy departments, nursing and technicians, other clinical specialties and patients; when cases or procedures exceed one's practice scope or ability, or there are infection control hazards or equipment anomalies, pause the procedure, review the records and consult, refer or report according to policy.

Collaboration of adjacent and related positions: pathology and clinical staff read slides and discuss together; surgery collaborates with anesthesia and ward teams; internal medicine has two-way referral with specialty clinics; nursing collaborates with physicians and patients; technicians collaborate with physicians and equipment maintenance; within aesthetic medicine institutions, work is divided under the attending physician responsibility system.
Conclusion boundaries

This page is on the U.S. O*NET-SOC 29-1213.00 basis: the work definition includes disease diagnosis and treatment and possible dermatologic surgery functions; aesthetic medicine is only one part of it and has additional qualification and authorization requirements in different jurisdictions, and this page does not treat aesthetic procedures as the occupation's default work content.

The preparation levels, licences and authorization requirements of adjacent and related positions cannot be applied to this occupation, nor can this occupation's qualification substitute for another specialty's authorization; specific requirements must be verified item by item against the target jurisdiction's regulations, registered practice scope and the employing institution's policies.

The six verification items cover the diagnostic basis, missing history items, scope authorization, jurisdictional qualification, statistical basis and work environment. They are editorial questions for career exploration, and care is confirmed by qualified and authorized personnel using real materials.

The U.S. SOC classification and Chinese registered specialties cannot be swapped directly; degree, qualification, registration, training and institutional authorization are verified separately. Direction within the occupation: medical dermatology (common and chronic outpatient conditions)

Complete skin, hair and nail examination, lesion morphology records and differential considerations, manage acne, eczema and atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, infectious skin disease and hair and nail disorders long term, prescribe topical and systemic medication and monitor adverse reactions, and provide sun protection and skin self-examination education.

Editorial comparison: medical dermatology focuses on diagnosis, medication management and follow-up, with procedure volume, consultation length and patient numbers verified by institution; direction names must not be used to rank more patients or fewer procedures. Suspicious lesions are assessed by an authorized physician using actual materials to decide the examinations, biopsy and follow-up needed.

If you are willing to track the same group of chronic disease patients long term, are good at capturing key signs in limited time and enjoy repeated education, medical dermatology can be the main line.
Direction within the occupation: dermatologic surgery and skin tumours

Judge biopsy and surgical indications, perform skin biopsy, excision of superficial masses and procedures such as Mohs surgery, manage the perioperative period and wounds, organise skin cancer screening and follow-up of high-risk groups, and read slides with the pathology department to confirm margins.

Editorial comparison: dermatologic surgery involves surgery, specimens and perioperative records and requires the corresponding training and authorization; the subcategory's overall 65% consequence-of-error figure must not be interpreted as surgical risk being highest within the occupation. Whether complex reconstruction is referred depends jointly on the condition, ability and authorization.

If you are patient about procedural precision, can bear the risk of missed diagnosis and recurrence, and are willing to build up experience in procedures and margin judgment over the long term, you can plan for the dermatologic surgery and skin tumour direction.
Direction within the occupation: dermatopathology and difficult diagnosis

Compared with the other directions, the output shifts from treatment procedures to diagnostic opinions and pathology reports, with responsibility concentrated on interpretive accuracy and reporting time limits; it requires long-term collaboration with pathology and oncology and often involves difficult case consultation and teaching.
If you would rather do interpretation, comparison and reasoning and are happy to take on consultation and teaching tasks, you can move toward dermatopathology and difficult diagnosis.
Adjacent occupations: pathologists (physicians-pathologists) and general practitioners (family-medicine-physicians)

The O*NET pathology profile includes microscopic specimen analysis, reporting, consultation and biopsy sampling, so it cannot be said that they do not directly manage patients; general practice first-contact care and long-term management and dermatology disease care have different divisions by position, and tasks and outputs are compared rather than using whether patients are seen as the only boundary.

If you prefer interpretation and microscope work, compare the pathology direction; if you want to cover a broader range of health problems and take first-contact responsibility, compare the general practice direction.
Adjacent occupations: registered nurses (registered-nurses) and physician assistants (physician-assistants)

Registered nurses assess care needs and form nursing plans; physician assistants can take on care and some prescribing and similar tasks, with O*NET outlining the physician supervision framework, and actual authority must be verified against the target jurisdiction. Nursing, PA and dermatology qualifications do not automatically substitute for each other, and the U.S. overview is not applied nationwide to China or to all states.
If you prefer clinical execution and patient care, compare the nursing path; if you want to take on clinical work within a physician collaboration framework, compare the physician assistant path.
Boundary note: medical aesthetics and aesthetic dermatology procedures

An aesthetic dermatology attending physician must simultaneously have licensed physician qualification and registration, at least 3 years of clinical experience in dermatology, qualified medical aesthetics training or further study or at least 1 year of clinical work in medical aesthetics, plus other provincial conditions. The 2016 amendment makes clear that a licensed physician not meeting the attending conditions may provide medical aesthetics clinical technical services under the attending physician's direction, and this is not a basis for those without physician qualification to provide care. The 2017 notice has medical institutions determine the attending specialty and file with the issuing department; individual specialty filing and institutional diagnosis and treatment subjects and project admission are verified separately.

If the goal includes aesthetic dermatology procedures, verify item by item before job seeking and practice whether you meet the attending physician conditions and whether the institution has completed project filing and surgical authorization, rather than entering the field by institution name.

The directions explain differences and do not mean the same practitioner can practise across directions; the specific scope follows practice qualification, registered practice scope, training experience and unit authorization.

Direction choice should depend on the types of patients and responsibilities you are willing to take on long term, not on institution names or a single wage figure; the training experience and authorization scope of the directions within the occupation differ, and the qualifications of adjacent occupations cannot substitute for each other.

Technical capability, actual adoption, job outcomes and replacement probability are four different questions; this page does not pass one off as another.

It can assist in generating image prompts, record summaries and draft follow-up data compilations, but these must be checked item by item against the skin, hair and nail examination, the original lesion images and the pathology results before being used for diagnosis and treatment decisions.

Article 13 sets out the registration procedures, and article 14 sets the registration location, category and scope; the qualification examination and registration are separate; article 24 requires personal examination and investigation and timely completion of medical documents as required, and prohibits concealing, forging, altering or destroying them without authorization; article 25 verifies general disclosure separately from the risks, alternatives and explicit consent for surgery, special examinations and special treatments. The Chinese Medical Doctor Association's 2022 dermatology residency guidelines: 36 months including 3 months of flexibility, not 36 plus 3; Year 1 covers comprehensive clinical ability, Year 2 dermatology and venereology foundations and Year 3 intensification, with tiered supervision such as full or partial supervision. The training objectives include diagnosis and treatment of common diseases, records, biopsy and simple excision of superficial masses, and completion does not automatically grant all surgical, pathology reporting or aesthetic authority; admission and individual adjustments are verified separately, and the order of examination, registration and entry into training is not standardised.

Where medical aesthetics applies, article 11 requires the aesthetic dermatology attending physician to have licensed physician qualification and registration and more than 3 years of dermatology clinical experience, with qualified medical aesthetics training or further study, or more than 1 year of aesthetic medicine clinical experience, plus other provincial conditions; the training and the 1-year branch are alternative, and the remaining conditions are cumulative. The 2017 notice has the institution determine the attending specialty, file with the department issuing the institution's certificate and note it on the certificate, with the original registration information unchanged. Article 29 provides that aesthetic activities involved in the treatment of diseases in the relevant clinical disciplines do not fall under these measures, so all disease-treatment lasers cannot be classified uniformly as aesthetic attending work. De-identification is not anonymization, and an institutional account does not authorize uploading to external AI. Article 19 of the medical aesthetics measures separately requires written disclosure of indications, contraindications, risks and precautions and the signed consent of the patient or guardian; article 20 prohibits disclosing related medical records and so on to third parties without their consent, and the general information processing basis cannot be used to dilute this specific requirement.

Periods and scopes are not mixed, a net increase is not the same as average annual openings, and the projection is not AI causation or an individual hiring probability.
